title: Adaptive urgency-window negotiation and ephemeral checkpointing for interrupted streaming generations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: When clients disconnect or experience network jitter during long-running streaming generations (including function/tool invocation sequences), we currently choose between aggressive GC (losing useful partial output) or preserving state long-term (costly). There is no standardized way for clients to express urgency or recoverability of an in-progress generation, nor do SDKs consistently interoperate when negotiating flow-control windows across HTTP streaming, SSE, and gRPC. This ticket designs and implements: 1) a compact "urgency window" in the stream-handshake where clients optionally provide an urgency score and desired persistence TTL for partial snapshots; 2) server-side adaptive windowing that adjusts token-supply / batch sizing based on urgency, observed latency, and concurrency; 3) ephemeral per-generation checkpointing (small snapshots of KV/prefix state) with tombstone TTLs and deterministic resume handshake; 4) an SDK compatibility shim so older SDKs gracefully fallback to default windows and still receive soft-abort semantics. Goal: reduce lost useful partial outputs on disconnects by 70% for high-urgency requests while keeping incremental storage cost under a 5% delta for typical workloads.
motivation: Provide predictable semantics for interrupted streams and make recovery practical for product use-cases: toolchains that perform multi-step function calls, long-form content generation, and structured output pipelines. Offer engineers clear levers (urgency score + TTL) to trade cost vs. recoverability.
design_notes: - Handshake: extend existing streaming init frame with optional fields: urgency (0-10), preferred_checkpoint_ttl (seconds). These are advisory; server overrides are possible. - Server policy: map urgency -> min_window_size and checkpoint_frequency. High urgency -> smaller batches, more frequent lightweight checkpoints retained for the requested TTL. Low urgency -> larger batches, opportunistic checkpoints only at stable boundaries. - Checkpoints: store compact descriptors (prefix KV pointers, position cursor, minimal function-call context hashes) rather than full cache blobs to reduce storage. - Tombstones: checkpoints expose a tombstone id; upon client resume, the SDK presents tombstone id + client generation id; server validates deterministic resume. - SDK shim: for legacy SDKs, add a compatibility header 'X-RI-Stream-Compat: v1' and fallback semantics: server uses conservative defaults and emits a soft-abort event with a short-lived resume token. - Observability: emit metrics for urgency distribution, checkpoint-store occupied bytes, resume success rate, and per-urgency lost-output rate.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Protocol: streaming handshake accepts optional urgency and ttl fields; server persists checkpoints for requests with ttl>0. 2) Server: adaptive windowing adjusts at runtime (based on measured latency and concurrency) and respects urgency mappings documented in the design doc. 3) SDK: JS and Python SDKs implement the compatibility shim and resume handshake. 4) Tests: automated unit and integration tests covering resume success, incompat shim fallback, and GC tombstone expiry. 5) Metrics: dashboards created showing lost-output rate reduced for high-urgency traffic by >70% in canary traffic. 6) No regression in p50/p95 latency beyond 5% for standard workloads.
test_plan: - Unit tests for handshake parsing and checkpoint serialization. - Integration tests: simulate intermittent network disconnects with deterministic RNG; assert resume recovers partial tokens and function-call state for 90%+ of high-urgency trials. - Load tests: run canary with 1% traffic on dedicated pool; measure additional checkpoint storage and p95 latency. - Chaos tests: client replays with mismatched tombstone ids to validate safe rejection and cleanup. - Cross-SDK compatibility matrix tests: HTTP streaming (fetch/stream), SSE, and gRPC.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged server rollout to canary region (us-west-2) and internal tenants. 2) Publish SDK minor releases (js/pypi) with compatibility header. 3) Monitor key metrics for 48h: checkpoint-store growth, resume success, latency regressions. 4) Gradual ramp to 25% traffic over one week, then global GA once metrics stable. 5) Provide migration guide for customers that want custom persistence TTLs.
risks: - Storage growth if many clients request long TTLs; mitigated by global quota enforcement and per-customer caps. - Determinism: if function-call side-effects are non-idempotent, resume may be complex; design enforces resumable checkpoints only for idempotent function-call patterns or provides explicit soft-abort. - SDK fragmentation: older SDKs might ignore headers; compatibility shim reduces risk but requires documentation. - Security: resume tokens must be unforgeable; use HMAC with per-tenant keys via KMS.
implementation_notes: - Back-end: new streaming-agent module implements adaptive-window controller and checkpoint manager. - Storage: use optimized LRU-backed object store with per-tenant quotas; metadata stored in fast key-value index. - Tokens: resume tokens are HMAC-signed with tenant key and include tombstone id + expiry. - API: handshake fields are backward-compatible (optional) and validated server-side. - Dev docs: add an RFC to the repo and a Confluence page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/STREAM-URGENCY-RFC.
